scene parrotpicture2
scene futabanodokabook1
: What the fuck is this?
: Uh-oh.
: Well, hello Futaba. You’re looking lovely tonight.
: Nodoka, what the fuck is this?
: I believe that is called a “book.”
scene futabanodokabook2
: Nodoka!
: You don’t have to yell. I’m right here. You asked what it was and I told you what it was. I’m not sure what else you want from me.
: I want to know what possessed you to write this! That’s what!
scene futabanodokabook3
: Artistic vision, I suppose? The endless font of creativity that is my brain? The abundance of hormones flowing through my body like blood due to living in a dorm with nineteen other girls?
: The possibilities are endless. Anything could have compelled me to write that book. The motivation matters not, though. It’s the story itself that I want people to dissect.
: I know the story already. That’s why I want to know why you’re doing this.
: Because it’s interesting, obviously. I wanted to try a new approach to things.
scene futabanodokabook4
: And, based on the fact that you bought it, it looks like I’ve succeeded. Thank you very much for supporting my work, Futaba. It means a lot to me.
: Is this a joke to you? Do you not see how serious I am right now?
: I see exactly how serious you are. But I also know that it’s only a matter of time until everything clicks and you realize that this is, in no way, meant to be malicious or evil.
: Tell me, how far into the book did you make it before you stormed over to my room? You’re the first person involved who’s actually read it, so I’m genuinely curious.
: Otoha, get out.
scene futabanodokabook5
: Yup. Bye.
: I can’t believe you...Why would you do something like this?
: Has your creativity dried up? Have you gotten so tired of coming up with your own stories that you had to steal ours instead?
: Quite the opposite, actually. And it’s not as if my new series is a perfect retelling. I can’t be everywhere at once, of course.
: Some...creative liberties needed to be taken to compensate for things I wasn’t present for.
scene futabanodokabook6
: I have known you for a very long time, Nodoka. I’ve seen you make questionable decisions and I, more than anyone, understand what type of person you are.
: I am sensing a disconnect between your words and your actions right now. If you understand, what’s there to get so up in arms over?
: I have stuck up for you countless times. I’ve fought for you when no one else “got it.” And I’ve been calling you one of my biggest inspirations for years.
scene futabanodokabook7
: But this?...I don’t understand. Why?
: I believe “Why not?” is just as valid of a question here if you’re unable to come up with an answer yourself, Futaba. What do you believe is wrong about writing a story based on one’s experiences?
scene futabanodokabook8
: Is that not one of the many methods of tackling fiction?
: Drawing parallels between real life and make-believe worlds? Connecting them in new, thought-provoking ways? Teaching people lessons they’d never learn otherwise?
: For what reason would I not write this book? There’s simply far too much I’m able to teach with its concept for me to just overlook it or actively decide against it.
: It’s an invasion of privacy, Nodoka. I don’t want my whole life inside one of your books. And that’s not even mentioning how anyone else would feel if they read this...
scene futabanodokabook9
: Then I suppose I should be happy that it’s only you and I who regularly read. Besides, I’m sure the unnamed masses will take something from it. It doesn’t need to be us per se.
: It’s just...it feels so...invasive. And I’m only three chapters in.
: Oh, wow. So you haven’t even gotten to the good parts yet. I’ll have to put that in my notes.
: You’re really going to keep going through with this?
: Of course. You haven’t given me a good reason not to yet.
scene futabanodokabook10
: Then...if I say I’ll stop talking to you if you follow through with this...is that a good enough reason?
: Good? No. Threatening? Yes. Losing you is an outcome I’d like to avoid if at all possible. But I also believe I know you well enough by now to ascertain that this is a bluff of sorts.
: I believe the whole truth is that you will do absolutely nothing if I continue to publish this book as doing so would go against your character.
scene futabanodokabook11
: You only know that because I am just a character to you, aren’t I?! I’m just a pawn you can move around in your book to keep your story interesting!
: If you actually cared about me, you wouldn’t...dehumanize all of us like this!
: You’re likely only saying that because you haven’t reached your character’s introduction yet. Read that before condemning me as some sort of malicious chess master.
scene black
: Fine. Where do I-
: Page 99. Much of the book is a blur to me as it was written while I was mentally exploding, but I remember that one.
: Hah...
: Fubuki was a breath of fresh air — a lone butterfly in an eclipse of moths. But if you asked her, she’d likely tell you she was nothing more than a caterpillar.
: Despite that, she wasn’t the type of girl to stand out in a crowd. She didn’t need to be, though.
: In fact, it was probably better she clung to the background as it meant my eyes could taint her the most.
: But...even with that said...she was so pure and so beautiful that it would take...years of gazing into hers to make even the slightest change...
: Nodoka, this doesn’t-
: Keep reading.
: Hah...She had trouble accepting love because she felt it was misdirected. But the only reason she felt that way at all was...was because of the eclipse...
: She’d spent so long among the moths that...each flap of her wings served not to guide her deeper into the mouth of the sky, but...further away from the light the others flocked to.
: The sad reality at play here is that she would have glowed brighter than any of them. That she would stand out if she only allowed herself to...
: But alas...the scourge of undesired uniqueness makes it harder to break free from refurbished chrysalides. And so the...never-ending cycle of misplaced doubt went down with the moon-
: Only to rise again the following night.
scene futabanodokabook12
: How I long to be a new light — one that guides her to the deepest lakes of sugar water so she can drink in me and feel renewed.
: If only those wings would stop getting caught on themselves...if only I was brighter.
: That wasn’t all bad, was it?
scene futabanodokabook13
: No...it was very sweet. But it changes nothing, Nodoka. You did this without even talking to any of us.
: Why would I do that? You’d all just refuse to participate and then I wouldn’t have a book at all.
scene futabanodokabook14
: That’s the whole point! You’re doing something that you know none of us would agree to, and yet you’re not seeing any sort of issue with it!
: Yes, because it isn’t up to any of you to determine what I do or do not write. If something piques my interest, I’m inclined to dive further into it. I assumed you’d know that by now.
: I do, but that doesn’t mean I have to like it!
: I’m confused. No one is asking you to like it. And it seems as if you’re taking exception to the existence of such a trait all on its own.
: That trait is fine when it’s not causing you to spill all of our secrets into a book! This doesn’t do any good for anyone but you!
: It’s not as if I’m exempt from exposing my secrets as well, Futaba. There’s no author bias here. I’ll be just as naked as the rest of you come the final installment.
scene futabanodokabook15
: But Nodoka...none of us should be naked. Our secrets are meant to be secrets. They’re not building blocks for your fictional exposé.
: They quite literally are though.
: What?
scene futabanodokabook16

: Well, the idea of an exposé is to reveal the true nature of something. So even if you tack a prefix like “fictional” onto it, it’s still fulfilling a key purpose by bringing a certain truth to light.
: And truth is determined by history. Which is determined by specific examples and accounts from real life events.
: But I suppose things get muddier when there is an assumption to be made about truth in the context of a fictional world.
: What?...I didn’t understand any of that.
: Sorry, I’m trying to figure out a way to explain it that would be coherent to someone else.
scene futabanodokabook17
: But I suppose the gist is that the “secrets” you and everyone else share are the closest I can get to examples and accounts of real life happenings.
: Which could then become building blocks to better lay out my fictional reconstruction of our reality so it can be shared and understood by people who aren’t with us to experience it firsthand.
: Why do other people have to experience it at all? Why can’t it just be for us?
: Because people like us live for this. We need stories like this to exist because life isn’t interesting unless we can compare and contrast it with a fabricated version.
: Out of the hundreds of books you’ve read, I’d wager at least half of them were someone’s reality at some point. What I do is no different from that. You’re just on the opposite end for once.
: Nodoka, I don’t like being on the opposite end. I don’t want people to know how I feel or what I’m doing. And I’m afraid of what will happen to me if people find out.
: Then why are you doing such a piss poor job of hiding it all?
scene futabanodokabook18
: Excuse me?

: I’m just not sure I understand the rationale behind revealing your truths to someone else if you don’t want anyone to know those truths. It’s no longer a secret once it crosses your tongue, correct?
: So because I shared something with you...something I told you in confidence because you are my friend...it means that I don’t understand what a secret is? That I want everyone else to know?
: But...no one else knows. All I did was use your experiences to create new ones for someone else. And if that someone else is a product of my imagination, shouldn’t I be able to share those things?
scene futabanodokabook19

: No! Because it’s not someone else! It’s us! It’s me! That’s what I’ve been trying to tell you this whole time! So you’re either trying to manipulate me right now or you just flat out lack common sense!
: Which one of those two do you think it is?
: I don’t care which one it is! I just want it to stop!
: Then stop clutching the book so close to your chest and just burn it or something. No one is forcing you to read it. That’s a decision you made yourself.
scene futabanodokabook20
: In fact, I’d urge you to stop reading it if the first three chapters were enough to impact you to this extent. It only gets messier from then on, Futaba.
: I’m sure you know that already, though. But hey, maybe if you do continue, you’ll enjoy seeing things from someone else’s perspective as it will show you just how everyone else views you.
: I seriously can’t believe you...you’re not getting it at all. You don’t see any problem with this.
: I see that...you have a problem with it. And acknowledge that others directly involved may as well.
: But I’d also implore all of those people, yourself included, to remember that this book is just, for lack of a better word-
: A rectangle.
: And it will remain a rectangle until someone comes along and sees it as anything else.
: Unbelievable...You’re seriously unbelievable.
scene futabanodokabook21
: See, this is precisely why I never make a big deal out of anything I do. No one else ever looks at things the same way as me.
: It’s incredibly exhausting never getting through to people when that is quite literally my job.
: You know what else is exhausting? Having a best friend who cares more about herself than your feelings.
scene futabanodokabook22
: Would you not do the same? Just because you prioritize yourself over someone else doesn’t mean that you don’t love them.
scene futabanodokabook23
: And I-
: ...Futaba?
: Why are you crying? Was it something I said?
: I hope you’re happy, Nodoka.
: I really hope you are.
scene futabanodokabook24
: Futaba, wait. I don’t think you’re necessarily understanding what-
scene futabanodokabook25
scene futabanodokabook26
: Huh.
scene black
